articles.title: Knicks become first defending NBA champions to begin season 0-2 in 15 years, lose 107-103 to Celtics
articles.summary: The last reigning NBA champs to begin the next season with two consecutive defeats were the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks lost their second consecutive game to open the 2026-27 season, falling to the Boston Celtics at TD Garden on Friday, 107-103 .

With the defeat, the Knicks became the first defending NBA champions to begin the next season 0-2 since the Dallas Mavericks started 0-3 to tip off the 2011-12 campaign. (Some might say the Knicks are off to an 0-3 start with their empty ring box shenanigans with the team's coaches before losing their season opener on Tuesday.)

Jayson Tatum led the Celtics to a win in their home opener with 36 points, hitting two key baskets in the final 1:24 of the fourth quarter to build a five-point lead after the Knicks cut their deficit to 99-98. His 3-pointer with 30.3 seconds remaining effectively put the game away.

Tatum added 9 rebounds, 7 assists and 3 steals in a strong all-around performance. Paul George followed with 15 points and 7 boards, while Neemias Queta scored 15 with 6 rebounds and 3 blocks for the Celtics.

The first half was tight with New York taking a 27-26 first-quarter lead as Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby each scored eight points. But George hit a 3-pointer from the left corner to put Boston ahead 50-49 going into halftime.

The Celtics pulled away in the third quarter, going on a 12-3 run midway during the first five minutes of the frame and outscoring the Knicks 8-2 to take a 10-point lead into the closing 12 minutes of the game.

Boston boosted its lead to 12 points three different times during the fourth quarter before Towns and Landry Shamet led a 9-0 Knicks run to trim the Celtics' lead to 94-91 with four minutes remaining in regulation.

A 3-pointer from Josh Hart followed by a pull-up jumper by Jalen Brunson put New York within one point before Tatum hit consecutive shots to make it a two-possession game.

Towns scored 22 points for the Knicks with 10 rebounds, while Anunoby added 20 points and grabbed 10 boards. Brunson followed with 19 points, but shot 7-for-17 from the floor and had 4 assists to 3 turnovers. Hart finished with 10 points and 12 rebounds.

During the previous five NBA seasons, the reigning league champions got off to the following starts:

Oklahoma City Thunder: 8-0 ( eventually starting 24-1 ) Boston Celtics: 4-0 Denver Nuggets: 4-0 Golden State Warriors: 1-1 Milwaukee Bucks: 1-1

The Knicks return to Madison Square Garden on Sunday to pursue their first win of the season versus the Orlando Magic. The Celtics are off for two days before continuing their four-game homestand by hosting the Chicago Bulls.

articles.title: Mitchell Robinson Reveals Why He Didn't Watch Knicks' NBA Title Ring Ceremony After Celtics Opener
articles.summary: Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson revealed during an interview with NBA on Prime Video's Cassidy Hubbarth why he didn't watch the championship ring ceremony of his former team, the New York Knicks. In essence, it was for practical reasons.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics center Mitchell Robinson revealed during an interview with NBA on Prime Video's Cassidy Hubbarth why he didn't watch the championship ring ceremony of his former team, the New York Knicks. In essence, it was for practical reasons.

"I didn't have cable. We just came back from Detroit, and I don't have the channels on my phone and stuff like that," Robinson said.

When Hubbarth jokingly noted that this was part of the "moving process," Robinson agreed, with a smile.

In fairness to Robinson, watching the ceremony live may not have been convenient. The ceremony took place around 6:30-7 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Earlier in the afternoon, the Celtics visited Detroit for a 3 p.m. battle with the Pistons. The home team won, 121-113, and then the Celtics had to get ready and head back to Boston. In theory, Robinson could have perhaps multi-tasked, but he had business to attend to, ultimately.

Robinson played eight seasons on the Knicks and helped the team win the NBA title last year thanks to his strong rebounding, tenacious defense and infectious energy. He left in free agency for the C's, signing a three-year, $47.4 million contract.

It's clear there's still love between Robinson and the Knicks, as evidenced by the big man's comments that he still loves his old teammates. As Hubbarth noted, Knicks wing Josh Hart still saves Robinson's seat in film sessions.

Robinson faced his old Knicks team on Friday evening in Boston. The C's were victorious, 107-103, and Robinson started and played 22 minutes, posting four points, four rebounds, two assists and a block.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Drops Viral Quote on Jaylen Brown Drama After 76ers Star Calls 'Cap' on Trade Reaction
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum explained that he doesn't feel any animosity towards Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown, his former Boston Celtics teammate.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum explained that he doesn't feel any animosity towards Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown, his former Boston Celtics teammate.

"For me, I understand we're in the entertainment business," Tatum told reporters Friday. "Me personally, I'm not much of an off the court entertainer type of guy. For me, I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him. I think the frustrating part is since he's not with the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven't been enough about what we've accomplished. All the games we've won, winning a championship, how we've grown together. It's turned into this drama type of thing."

"I reached out to him the day he got traded," he added. "I called him, I texted him. I understand people process things differently. At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed X, Y, and Z like on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have that."

Tatum added: "This ain't no f--king Shaq and Kobe."

After Tatum previously posted a video in which he explained that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by the offseason trade between the Celtics and 76ers involving Brown, his old teammate responded with a cap emoji .

On July 1, Philadelphia acquired Brown from Boston in exchange for Paul George, two first-round draft picks and two second-round picks.

The change of scenery occurred after the Celtics reportedly offered Brown in trade negotiations for Giannis Antetokounmpo, but the Milwaukee Bucks ultimately dealt the two-time MVP to the Miami Heat.

After Boston's trade with Philadelphia was finalized, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the off-court relationship between Brown and Tatum was "as close to non-existent as you could have" over the past year.

Brown revealed that he had yet to speak with Tatum about the trade during his introductory press conference on Aug. 6 and admitted they had their "ups and downs," but also explained that he still had "respect" for his former teammate.

Brown and Tatum's shared tenure in Boston was from 2017-26, as the Celtics made the playoffs in every season across that span. They combined to earn 11 All-Star nods during that time.

The duo helped lead the Celtics to a championship in 2024, with Brown taking home Finals MVP honors.

The Celtics and 76ers will face off for the first time during the 2026-27 season on Nov. 10.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Takes Over Late as Celtics Defeat Knicks
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics earned an impressive 107-103 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday night, using a dominant third quarter and a clutch performance fro...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics earned an impressive 107-103 victory over the New York Knicks on Friday night, using a dominant third quarter and a clutch performance from Jayson Tatum to secure their first home win of the 2026-27 NBA season.

Tatum delivered one of his strongest performances of the young season, finishing with 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. After a relatively quiet first half, the Celtics star took control after halftime, scoring 25 of his points in the second half and delivering several crucial baskets down the stretch.

Paul George and Neemias Queta also contributed 15 points apiece, helping Boston withstand a late push from the defending NBA champion Knicks.

Celtics Build Momentum in the Third Quarter

The opening half featured plenty of back-and-forth action, with neither team able to create much separation. New York held a narrow 49-50 deficit at halftime after a competitive first two quarters that included multiple lead changes.

Boston found another gear coming out of the locker room. The Celtics outscored the Knicks 33-24 in the third quarter, creating breathing room heading into the final period.

Tatum led the charge, attacking the basket and finding opportunities to score from the perimeter. Boston's offense became more efficient, while its defense made it difficult for New York to maintain consistency.

The Celtics eventually built their advantage to 91-79, putting themselves in position to close out the game.

New York refused to go away quietly. The Knicks put together a 12-3 run to cut Boston's lead to 94-91, setting up a tense finish at TD Garden.

After the Knicks continued to threaten, Tatum answered with a difficult jumper to restore some separation. He followed that with another important basket before knocking down a three-pointer late in the fourth quarter.

Those shots proved critical as Boston held off the Knicks' comeback attempt and secured the four-point victory.

Karl-Anthony Towns led New York with 22 points and 10 rebounds, while OG Anunoby recorded 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Deuce McBride also scored 20 points off the bench, and Jalen Brunson finished with 19.

The victory improved Boston's record to 1-1, giving the Celtics an important early-season boost against a conference rival.

Tatum's late-game execution was the biggest takeaway, particularly with the Knicks threatening to steal the game in the final minutes.

Boston will look to carry that momentum into its next matchup against the Chicago Bulls on Monday night.

articles.summary: Atlanta Hawks guard Dyson Daniels is putting the NBA on notice after recording an incredible 12 steals in just two games, establishing himself as one of the...
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks guard Dyson Daniels is wasting no time reminding the NBA why he is considered one of the league's most disruptive perimeter defenders.

Through the first two games of the season, Daniels has already recorded an impressive 12 steals, demonstrating the defensive instincts, quick hands, and relentless effort that have made him a nightmare for opposing ball handlers.

While scoring performances typically dominate headlines around the NBA, Daniels is proving that defense can be just as impactful.

His ability to anticipate passing lanes, pressure opposing guards, and create turnovers has provided Atlanta with an important defensive presence early in the season.

For the Hawks, Daniels' production represents more than an impressive individual statistic. His defensive activity creates additional transition opportunities, allowing Atlanta to push the basketball and generate easier scoring chances.

Daniels recorded five steals in Atlanta's 132-125 season-opening victory over the Orlando Magic , finishing with 20 points, four rebounds, and three assists.

Daniels making case for defensive player of the year

He followed that performance with seven steals in Friday's dominant 128-81 victory over the Charlotte Hornets . Daniels also contributed 11 points, nine rebounds, and four assists as Atlanta improved to 2-0.

His 12 steals are the most by any NBA player through the first two games of a season this century.

Following Friday's victory, Daniels acknowledged that Charlotte made some costly mistakes.

"In this game they were just giving it to me, I'm not going to lie. They were throwing it in my hands," Daniels said.

The Australian guard's defensive performance is quickly becoming one of the biggest storylines surrounding Atlanta's undefeated start.

With Daniels leading the defensive charge, the Hawks are showing early signs of becoming a dangerous team in the Eastern Conference.

If Daniels maintains anything close to this production, another All-Defensive selection could be within reach.

For now, one thing is clear: opposing teams must be extremely careful whenever Daniels is guarding the basketball.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum downplays dispute with Jaylen Brown after contentious Instagram comment: 'This ain't no f***ing Shaq and Kobe'
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum would like everyone to stop making a big deal about his relationship with Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum would like everyone to stop making a big deal about his relationship with former teammate Jaylen Brown.

On Friday, the Boston Celtics star found himself once again discussing the trade that sent Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers and ended a nine-year partnership in Boston. Brown has made no secret about his displeasure over the trade .

That displeasure popped up in an Instagram comment section on Thursday night, in reaction to a video of Tatum saying he was as surprised as anyone by the trade. Brown's comment of only a single emoji: cap.

In other words, Brown was accusing Tatum of lying.

That's an awkward look, no matter how you cut it.

Tatum was asked about the comment after the Celtics' 107-103 win over the New York Knicks on Friday and did his best to downplay the drama to reporters , going so far as to invoke the infamous feud between Shaquille O'Neal and Kobe Bryant once the Los Angeles Lakers traded the former:

"This ain't no f***ing Shaq and Kobe. There's no beef. It's not about that. It should be more praise. I understand that don't necessarily sell and drama gets clicks and views, but that's not my thing."

The Brown trade, which netted Paul George and a collection of draft picks for the Celtics, is unusual in a few ways. Most unusual is a contender sending a 30-year-old All-Star to an Eastern Conference rival. Brown had also just carried the Celtics for much of the 2025-26 season while Tatum was recovering from an Achilles rupture.

Tatum and Brown won a championship together, but there were always questions about whether the Celtics wanted to carry two wings on supermax contracts in the long term, especially as Brown got older. Tatum still described the divorce as painful at the time .

On Friday, he tried explaining that he doesn't enjoy the drama in public, even if the comment from Brown's account is what got this started:

articles.title: Lakers Beat Clippers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Luka Doncic, Reaves, Kessler, Top Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers won their second straight game to begin the season on Friday after defeating the Los Angeles Clippers at home on Friday evening, 125-117.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers won their second straight game to begin the season on Friday after defeating the Los Angeles Clippers at home on Friday evening, 125-117.

Here's a look at notable performances from the 2-0 Lakers, who were 8.5 point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

The 1-1 Clippers dropped their first game after beating the Sacramento Kings 121-96 in the opener.

The Lakers and Clippers were tied 64 going into halftime. However, the Lakers dominated the third quarter, outscoring the Clips 39-26. That gave the Lakers enough of a cushion in the fourth quarter, where they led by double digits for most of it before a late Clipper run to cut the lead down to six.

The Lakers excelled despite an off-night from Luka Doncic, who shot 8-of-21 and committed a career-high 11 turnovers.

As always, though, Doncic remained productive with a 23-point, seven-assist, six-rebound night, and L.A. was plus-10 with him on the floor.

The Lakers shot 58 percent from the field and 44 percent from three. Lakers center Walker Kessler continued his incredible efficiency, scoring his 22 points on 10-of-14 shooting. He's now 22-of-26 on the year after making all 12 of his field goals in the Lakers' 127-105 season-opening win over the Golden State Warriors. Kessler also dominated defensively with nine combined blocks (six) and steals (three).

Austin Reaves also enjoyed an efficient evening, making 10-of-13 shots and 3-of-5 threes. Like Doncic, he struggled with turnovers (six), but his scoring output and assists (nine) more than made up for it in the victory.

Meanwhile, the Clippers fared well offensively when they got up shots, making 49 percent of their field goals and 43 percent of their three-pointers. However, the Clippers committed 25 turnovers, including nine from Darius Garland.

That being said, Garland scored 26 points, including six in a late 8-0 run that cut the Laker lead to 119-113 with 3:21 left. A six-point deficit was as close as the Clippers got down the stretch.

Clippers center Brook Lopez, in his 19th NBA season, posted 22 points on 8-of-9 shooting in just 20 minutes off the bench. Rookie guard Keaton Wagler added 13 points, and he's now averaging 14.0 PPG after a 15-point effort in the first game.

Both teams will hit the road on Sunday. The Lakers will visit the Utah Jazz, and the Clippers will play the Oklahoma City Thunder.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs have plenty to figure out after 0-2 start
articles.summary: An overreliance on their superstar and a new starter have the Spurs struggling to find their rhythm.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas — The subtle significance of Victor Wembanyama's potential game-tying layup attempt — resulting in an incredible block by Rockets wing Amen Thompson — should not be buried underneath the rubble of a surprising 0-2 start by the San Antonio Spurs.

It would be unwise and disingenuous to shovel the bulk of blame for San Antonio's sluggish showing on the Frenchman's sleek shoulders. Yes, he shot just 3-for-11 in the second half (9-for-21 from the field overall) and succumbed to opposing, wide-ranging physicality for the second time this week. These are simply more hurdles for the superstar to maneuver on the path to basketball immortality — similar to a handful of his Finals mishaps.

But the Spurs' overreliance on the 22-year-old in an attempt to override a season-opening embarrassment to Oklahoma City are symptoms of a lineup switch and three-guard approach that has yet to bear fruit.

"We made some mistakes that were very costly," Wembanyama said following the 114-110 loss at the Moody Center. "That's our problem. We work hard for a time and then we go away. But it was better [than last game]."

For all the potential problems San Antonio's three-pronged guard roulette can cause teams, Friday night was a prime example of the rough spots that still remain. The Spurs' starters were minus-11 in 11 minutes together , producing a meager offensive rating of 76.4 and a walloping minus-47 net rating. Narrowing that production down to new starter Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox, San Antonio lost their minutes by 12, with just six assists to four turnovers.

Their issue is two-fold. Outside of Wembanyama, there's not a true pecking order or offensive flow between the three guards, which can make things confusing in high-pressure moments. Fox was once again diminished in the final frame , both from usage and shot-creation standpoints, attempting just one shot compared to 10 combined from Castle and Harper.

Wembanyanma was naturally going to assume a more aggressive role after a subdued opener, which is another interesting angle given what we saw and heard in training camp and preseason about him becoming more of a playmaker. He logged just two assists on the evening, but they were arguably two of San Antonio's brightest possessions, with Wemby absorbing contact and attention before spraying out to Castle on the perimeter and again at the rim. As the season goes on, both Wembanyama and the coaching staff will need to find the optimal balance between his scorer and creator roles.

But stylistically, it's difficult to envision teams not packing the paint and not daring the Spurs to beat them from the outside — especially if Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie aren't utilized enough. Houston looked extremely comfortable sitting back, forming mini walls of obstruction, stunting on drives and embracing a perimeter onslaught that never truly came. Castle missed six of his nine attempts from deep, and Harper has now started the season making just one of his six 3-point shots.

"We want to live with some guys making some shots," Rockets head coach Ime Udoka said, "and help on others. They have some really good one-on-one players, and we felt we could show a crowd and make some plays there — and I think we did that. The plan was to keep their points in the paint low, and they can beat us from 3."

Perhaps it's still too early to make judgment calls on this brave new lineup. When it works, and it certainly will at some point, teams will be caught in the crosshairs of San Antonio's speed and downhill daggers. But the Spurs looked the most dangerous — and analytically speaking performed the best — when both Vassell and Champagnie were on the floor. There's a certain familiarity that comes with knowing teams can't simply load up in the box with two bona fide floor spacers on the perimeter, which in turn gives the Spurs a better balance. Small sample size or not, it's strange that a team as talented as San Antonio currently finds itself ranked 22nd in offensive efficiency, 17th in halfcourt points per play and 21st in effective field-goal percentage.

"I feel like we're comfortable with it," said Wembanyama, who finished with 25 points, 13 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 blocks. "We've finished games with this lineup before and in the playoffs as well. It's not a concern for us."

As the losses pile up, the questions will as well. This team holds itself in such high regard — as does the rest of the basketball world — but this is a different challenge, a new frontier to conquer. The more the Spurs' offensive output looks less like a multi-faceted unit and more like a battering ram, the less dangerous this group looks to its rivals. Wembanyama's gargantuan wingspan can only account for so much.

articles.title: Thompson y su taponazo a Wembanyama para ganar el partido
articles.standfirst: Amen Thompson protagoniza la jugada defensiva de la temporada con su acción ante 'Wemby'
articles.summary: Amen Thompson protagoniza la jugada defensiva de la temporada con su acción ante 'Wemby'
articles.body: Dos partidos y dos taponazos a Wembanyama. Y además, dos derrotas de los Spurs. Y encima las dos en casa. Ya es casualidad que el mismo año que el campeón arranca con dos decepciones (algo que no ocurría desde los Mavs de 2012), los finalistas sigan el mismo camino. Los dos equipos que dominaron sus respectivas conferencias han perdido terreno muy pronto ante sus máximos rivales. Esta vez fue Houston el que asaltó la casa de los Spurs que en este caso fue el Moody Center de Austin. Ganó 100-104 gracias a una acción defensiva. Sí, como lo leen, una defensa salvó el partido de los Rockets. Pero además fue una defensa ante Victor Wembanyama. El coloso de los Spurs, que ya se llevó un taponazo de Aday Mara en su estreno en un alley-oop arruinado por el español, se llevó otro que incluso dolió más. No fue un alley-oop, fue un reverso cerca del aro en el que el francés trató de dejar la bola en el aro de los Rockets. Hubiera sido el empate ya que la jugada tuvo lugar a dos segundos para el final y entonces ganaba Houston 100-102. Amen Thompson, 23 centímetros más pequeño que 'Wemby', se emparejó con él en lo que parecía un error de asignación. Trató de aguantar al francés en la pintura y logró un salto prodigioso para cerrarle la puerta. El 'timing' del salto, la clave en esta jugada, es extraordinario, casi perfecto. De otro forma no lo hubiera conseguido. Una jugada que ya opta a la mejor acción defensiva de la temporada, y faltan 80 partidos... Thompson además acabó con 20 puntos y 10 rebotes en una formidable noche. También hizo 20 puntos Kevin Durant y Alperen Sengun lideró a todos en los Rockets con sus 29 puntos, siete rebotes y siete asistencias. Wembanyama, derrotado al final, destacó con 25 puntos y 13 rebotes y Dylan Harper hizo 20 puntos en unos Spurs que, como los Knicks, aún no se han estrenado.

articles.title: Former NBA player says ‘many’ players secretly support President Trump
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom has never been shy about sharing his political views, and he believes plenty of his former NBA peers share them too. They just won’t say...
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom has never been shy about sharing his political views, and he believes plenty of his former NBA peers share them too. They just won't say so out loud.

In a new interview, the former Boston Celtics center claimed that "many" NBA players privately support the Republican Party and President Donald Trump. But according to Kanter Freedom, those players keep it to themselves because they're afraid of being "canceled" and "hated on" around the league.

During a recent interview with OutKick , Kanter Freedom claimed that he was "cancelled" by his teammates after he appeared on Fox News.

"In NBA circles, we don't talk about Fox News, we don't watch Fox News, and if you do, you will realize that you are going to get cancelled and you're going to get hated on," Kanter Freedom said.

However, Kanter Freedom also claimed that there are more right-leaning players in the NBA than people realize.

"But there are many people actually that supports the conservative movements, supports the Republican Party, uh, many of them actually supports President Trump, but just because of they know that they will get canceled and they will get hated on throughout the whole year, they're just hiding it," Kanter Freedom said. "I mean, you're not even allowed to say you watch Fox News."

He made a similar claim about his campaign against the WNBA's eligibility rules, which most recently led to him being denied entry to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals . Kanter Freedom said some former NBA colleagues have privately told him they support him, but won't do so publicly.

According to Kanter Freedom, those players told him "we cannot help you," but also said, "but now we understand what you're doing and we support you and we will pray for you."

"I don't want to give their name because I know, I just know that as soon as I expose their name, then there will be a lot of questions," Kanter Freedom said.

Kanter Freedom claims that one of the biggest reasons for the NBA's political climate is megastar LeBron James.

Earlier this week, Trump demanded an apology from James after the 76ers star appeared to practice his golf swing during the national anthem before his Philadelphia debut. Kanter Freedom backed the president , and he called James "the dictator of the NBA."

"But I mean, everybody knows LeBron James… I call him the dictator of the NBA. And I think President Trump said the best. You know, he disrespects our country and disrespects our flag," Kanter Freedom said.

He then suggested that the league will look very different once James is gone.

"LeBron James is the reason the NBA is woke still. I promise you, once he retires, NBA is not going to be as woke as now," Kanter Freedom said.

Of course, James has been one of the NBA's most prominent voices for more than two decades, and Kanter Freedom did not offer any evidence for his claims about the league's political makeup.

James, meanwhile, has not addressed Kanter Freedom's comments.

articles.title: These 5 NBA Teams Already Need a Trade
articles.summary: Although NBA trade season doesn't unofficially tip off until Dec. 15, a handful of teams need to be working the phones long before then.
articles.body:
Although NBA trade season doesn't unofficially tip off until Dec. 15, a handful of teams need to be working the phones long before then.

Think this is an overreaction to the opening kick of the 2026-27 regular season? Not so fast. Many of these squads would have made the list before Game No. 1. Their inclusion indicts the offseason and the overall approach.

Certain teams are, in fact, fresh entrants into this discussion. But even their inclusion isn't totally reflexive. They already had perceived weaknesses or issues. Our concerns have merely been confirmed. In one case, a team is throwing its hat in the ring entirely on its own.

Whatever the reason, the front offices running all these franchises should have been working the phones and group texts yesterday.

Meet the team that put itself here. ESPN's Shams Charania reported earlier today that the Golden State Warriors are exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, who is reportedly considering walking away from basketball as he deals with lingering effects from his postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).

Granted, we didn't need a Porziņģis health crisis to include the Warriors. They brought back the aging, injury-riddled core of a 37-win team, plus Yaxel Lendeborg and expect fans to believe that's perfectly fine because what else were they supposed to do?

That's a whole other can of worms we won't open here. For now, the Warriors need an able-bodied center— preferably one who stands taller than 6'6", is younger than 40 and can space the floor.

Porziņģis' contract can be the primary salary anchor that nets Golden State an upgrade. He makes $20 million this year and is guaranteed only $3 million next season, making his contract quasi-expiring.

It isn't clear how aggressive the Warriors will be in their trade pursuits. A starting center alone isn't saving them from what's shaping up to be a gap year . They might prefer acquiring Myles Turner a half-decade too late over going after a bigger name.

At this point, what they do isn't as important as actually doing anything at all. Otherwise, they might as well ditch all pretense and release a statement saying they're having 38-year-old Stephen Curry work from home for the rest of the season.

Harsher analysis would focus on why the New Orleans Pelicans belong here because they need to tear this directionless basketball team down. I won't do that. I know better than to think New Orleans' C-Suite would dare rip apart a core capable of peaking at, like, 34 wins. (At least they're starting Jeremiah Fears?)

If the Pelicans are going to give this roster a real shot at exceeding expectations, they need a starting-level big who can complement Zion Williamson and Derek Queen. The solution clearly isn't to play them together. Head coach Jamahl Mosley rolled out the Zion-Queen tandem for a total of five minutes on opening night.

Yves Missi is a nice center and looked fantastic on opening night, but he's almost assuredly not the answer. He doesn't have the hands, spacing capacity or dominant defensive aura to pair effectively with either Zion or Queen. The Pelicans are allowing 117.1 points per 100 possessions with Zion and Missi on the floor together since the latter entered the league. That's the equivalent of a 24th-ranked defense during this stretch.

New Orleans shouldn't view its need in the middle as a license to go bananas on the trade market. Forking over future first-round picks when the team has no clear path to title contention would be malpractice.

Then again, at least swinging big on a center would count as a plan—something the Pelicans don't seem to have right now.

Congratulations to Phoenix Suns team governor Mat Ishbia for " cleaning up that stench " in the locker room and replacing it with the Eau de Dumpster Fire fragrance they debuted on opening night in Portland.

There's a lot that could be wrong with this team, but the lack of high-volume three-point shooting stands out most.

Phoenix traded away more than 30 percent of last season's made triples when they shipped Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, to Charlotte in exchange for Miles Bridges. While Bridges does other (largely mediocre) things on the basketball court, stretching defenses isn't one of them. He drilled 148 triples in 77 appearances last season. Grayson Allen, by comparison, put down 159 treys in 26 fewer games.

This all says nothing of the Suns' clear need for a better passer than Devin Booker and Collin Gillespie. If only they had a 2033 first-round pick to dangle in search of a shooting and table-setting upgrade.

Unfortunately, they have neither that nor a time machine they can use to go back and get it. They also don't have a ton of matching salary options.

Booker is probably off limits. Rerouting Bridges already would be hysterical but is unlikely. Luke Kennard (Dec. 15), Mark Williams (Jan. 15), Collin Gillespie (Jan. 15), Jordan Goodwin (Jan. 15) and Dillon Brooks (Feb. 8) aren't trade-eligible until midseason. Moving Khaman Maluach would be a giant middle finger to the future.

That basically leaves Jalen Green. His $36.3 million salary is large enough to shop for an impact player, but underwater enough that the asset-strapped Suns will need to include sweeteners. Especially when factoring in his $36 million player option next season.

Do they have enough to get in the running for Darius Garland? Kyrie Irving? Jrue Holiday? Somebody, anybody, else? They need to find out.

Power Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup 🔢

Making a trade just for the sake of making a trade is almost never good practice. As long as they're not surrendering valuable draft equity, the Sacramento Kings are the greatest of all exceptions.

You could make the case that all five of their highest-paid players—Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine, De'Andre Hunter, Malik Monk, Keegan Murray—would rather be hooping elsewhere. The Kings would likely be willing to grant Sabonis, LaVine and Monk their wishes if other teams were genuinely interested. The same can probably be said for Hunter.

But league-wide perception of these contracts works against mass movement.

Hunter ($24.9 million expiring salary) and Monk (two years, $41.8 million) are hardly immovable. Their numbers aren't exactly small or especially desirable, either. Sabonis (two years, $94.1 million) and LaVine ($48.9 million expiring salary) are making so much that acquiring them is seen as prohibitive.

Still, the Kings feel listless as currently constructed. They don't have a ton of value to glean from playing LaVine and Sabonis, specifically, 30-plus minutes per game. While both might already be gone if they had suitors, Sacramento must sufficiently lower its bar before we can consider it trapped.

If it turns out the Kings are boxed into a coffin of their own design, a smaller move will do. Something, anything, just to refresh a roster that's depressing to think about.

If any team on this list gets the armchair-GM's green light to aggressively buy this early in the season, it's the Utah Jazz.

They needed an upgrade at center the moment they signed-and-traded Walker Kessler to the Los Angeles Lakers. That has only become more apparent following Jusuf Nurkić's right toe injury, which is serious enough to sideline him for at least a month.

Vacillating between Jaxson Hayes minutes and Jaren Jackson Jr.-at-the-5 lineups only gets the Jazz so far. The rebounding is already an issue—at both ends of the floor. And though using JJJ at center has its advantages versus plenty of matchups, it displaces him from his most effective defensive role.

Utah has the draft equity and matching salaries beyond its core players to dream and transact big . But it could take a while for bigger names to shake loose.

In the interim, guys like Moussa Diabaté, Dylan Cardwell and Daniel Gafford should all be available. Even a flier on Brook Lopez's expiring contract could go a long way. He's not a big-time rebounder himself, but his teams always board misses better with him on the floor, and he can stay closer to the rim while Jackson wreaks havoc everywhere else.
